title: [observability] Each Core lines figure carries its trend over the last 7 days, and the card draws it
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-cli/src/commands/loops.rs (the loop's storage sample: `Sampler`, sampled at the loop's start and hourly), crates/spawn-cli/src/storage.rs, crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql (`spawn_host_record` and the control fold's `host.storage` case), crates/spawn-cli/src/serve.rs's core-lines module (objective 084) and web/src/coreLines.ts.

This comes after objective 084 (the Core lines frame), which must be in the tree. Figures that 086–088 add get trends like the rest.

The problem (owner, 2026-11-12 13:30, repeated by the lead at 13:5x; sync/roadmap-effects.md, "Showing and alerting"). The Core lines card shows each figure only as it is now. The owner asked for each row to show "a small trend over 7 days": a figure inside its range but falling fast needs attention before it leaves the range. Only a few figures have a history today (the storage samples, the scorecard's days); most have none. So the loop keeps one, an hourly sample of every figure's value, and the card reads its trends from it.

Required behaviour.
(a) The loop records a `host.core_lines` sample through `spawn_host_record`: {"type": "host.core_lines", "values": {<key>: <value>}}, holding every figure of the answer that has a value, as `GET /api/core-lines` would give it at that moment. It records one at its start and then every `SPAWN_CORE_LINES_SAMPLE_SECS` (default 3600). The store accepts the shape (values an object) and folds it into no table. A sample that cannot be read or written is a line in the loop's log, never a failed pass.
(b) Every figure of `GET /api/core-lines` carries `trend`:
- one point {day (UTC, YYYY-MM-DD), value} for each UTC day of the last 7 (today and the 6 before) that has a sample carrying the figure;
- each point is that day's last such sample;
- points are oldest first;
- a figure with no samples has an empty list.
(c) web/src/coreLines.ts exports `trendView(figure)`, giving {points, change}:
- `points` are the trend's values;
- `change` runs from the first point to the last: "up <n>%" or "down <n>%" (n rounded, relative to the first point's size), "steady" under half a percent, and null with fewer than two points or a first point of 0.
coreLinesView's marks stay as 084 says them. The module keeps loading with node alone.
(d) The card draws each figure's points as a small line beside it, with the change as its title. Read off a screenshot.
No gate, integrator or deploy step reads the samples or the trends.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/090.sh, on 065's world with a real `spawn loop`. Host.core_lines samples of free disk are seeded at fixed UTC days: 8 days ago (outside the window), 6 days ago (100 GiB), 3 days ago (110 GiB), and yesterday twice (999 bytes at 01:00, then 120 GiB at 05:00). Checks:
- (1) Within 60 s, the loop records a host.core_lines sample with free disk's value and no null.
- (2) Through `GET /api/core-lines`:
  - free disk's trend is [6 days ago 100 GiB, 3 days ago 110 GiB, yesterday 120 GiB], then today's point from this loop's sample;
  - every figure carries a trend list.
- (3) Under node, trendView gives "up 20%", "down 25%", "steady", null for one point, null for a first point of 0, and empty for no trend. Over the answer, free disk's first three points are as seeded.
It fails with 1 on f41cbcc1: no sample, /api/core-lines answers 404, and there is no coreLines.ts. Its throwaway stacks 084's throwaway (sync/obj-090/throwaway.diff).

The product reason. A guardrail is most useful before it is crossed. A 7-day line beside each figure shows the owner which way each line is going, not only where it stands. Monitoring only.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/, web/test/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green (084 and 065 among them) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour:
- a spawn-postgres test that a host.core_lines record goes through the real store and one without values is refused;
- a loop sampler unit test (at start, then hourly, a failed write retried);
- a core-lines unit test of the trend (a day's last sample, a day without, outside the window);
- web/test cases of trendView.
